$comment: How each connector module reaches the application: `bundled` is compiled into the core, `module` is not part of the installer, `bridge` is a module that this release still compiles in (the release after makes it `module`). docs/connector-delivery.md explains the rule; app/pom.xml and scripts/size-report.mjs follow this file, and scripts/delivery.test.mjs keeps them in step.

budget.$comment: The most a bundled connector may add to the native core, in megabytes of image, unless it is listed in `exempt` with the reason it stays compiled in.

exempt.sql: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite are the first connections most people make; JSqlParser classifies every dialect.
exempt.kubernetes: A flagship connector; kept compiled in by decision.
exempt.ssh: A flagship connector, and SSH log files and runbooks depend on it.
exempt.mongodb: One of the most used databases.
exempt.aws: The generic AWS API tools carry a catalog of every service.

cassandra.why: The driver's own GraalVM substitutions need JNR, which this build excludes, so the native core can't be built with it; its driver stack is also heavier than the budget.

neo4j.why: Its driver stack (the Bolt driver, Netty and Reactor) is more than twice the budget of a bundled connector.

sql-oracle.why: The Oracle JDBC driver alone is about 30 MB of native image, ten times the budget of a bundled connector.

sql-sqlserver.why: The SQL Server JDBC driver is about 7 MB of native image, more than twice the budget of a bundled connector.

moduleOnly.$comment: Connectors that exist only as modules. Their code lives with their package under modules/<id> and is never compiled into a core, not even with all-bundled: each relies on something only a module host gives it.

clickhouse.why: It needs nothing of the core but the host's guarded HTTP client, and few first connections are to ClickHouse: as a module it costs the installer nothing.

duckdb.why: Its JDBC driver is a native library, which the native core can't load, and the files it opens are confined by the module host's sandbox.

h2.why: The H2 client opens its own sockets, which only the module host's TCP gate confines to the connection's host and port.

msaccess.why: UCanAccess and HSQLDB are a large stack for a file format few people use, and the files it opens are confined by the module host's sandbox.
